current_state_summary.primary_concern: Car payment at $573/mo is 26% of income — too high for a 1.5-month runway. RoboRide Phase 2 hitting in 2 months will compete for rideshare demand exactly when I need the income most.

threat_assessment.immediate: $573/mo car payment consumes more than a quarter of monthly income. With $2,612 in savings and $1,787/mo in expenses, any income interruption collapses the runway fast. The payment is the single biggest lever I have.
threat_assessment.horizon_2mo: RoboRide Phase 2 launches in Millfield. It won't wipe out rideshare overnight — 3% adoption means most rides still go to human drivers — but it will compress demand in my operating zones, probably starting with airport and long-haul surges, which are my highest-yield slots. I need to earn hard now, before that softens.
threat_assessment.horizon_6mo: This is where the plan resolves. If I finish the nursing program on schedule, I'm entering the job market as an RN with a 796 credit score and zero identity attachment to rideshare. The $35,485 in debt is manageable on a $60-72K salary. The bridge is the hard part — not the destination.

actions.description: Contact my credit union this week to formally inquire about refinancing the car loan. I have a 796 credit score — I should not be carrying a $573/mo payment. Even dropping it to $420-$450/mo frees $120-$150 monthly, which extends runway by several weeks. I'll pull my current loan terms, get a competing quote, and initiate the refi application if the numbers work.
actions.rationale: This is the single highest-leverage action available to me right now. I don't need to sell the car — I need the car for both driving income and clinical rotations. But I'm almost certainly paying a rate that my current credit score no longer justifies. Refinancing doesn't change my income or expenses structurally; it just removes friction. With 796 credit, I should be able to get this done without a credit inquiry that hurts my score materially.
actions.timeline: This week — initiate inquiry Monday, have comparison quotes by Wednesday, submit application by Friday if rate differential is 1.5% or greater
actions.expected_outcome: Reduce monthly car payment by $100-$150, extending runway by 0.2-0.3 months. Not dramatic, but it's real cash freed from a fixed cost that was never optimized.

actions.description: Shift rideshare strategy from peak-hour maintenance to aggressive pre-launch maximization. For the next 8 weeks before RoboRide Phase 2 hits, I will add one additional block per week — specifically targeting Thursday evening and Sunday morning airport runs, which have historically had thin rideshare supply. I'll track earnings per zone weekly to detect early softening and adjust.
actions.rationale: The 2-month window before RoboRide Phase 2 is a known asset. Once AV adoption starts competing with my high-yield slots, my hourly rate drops. The logical move is to front-load income now while demand is still mine to capture. Adding roughly 6-8 hours per week at peak rates should generate an additional $90-$120 per tick. That goes directly to savings — I'm not changing my expenses, just building buffer before the squeeze.
actions.timeline: Starting this week, run through the 8-week pre-launch window. Reassess at the 4-week mark based on earnings data.
actions.expected_outcome: Savings increase of $280-$340 this tick instead of last tick's $206. Runway extends to approximately 1.7-1.8 months if refinancing also completes. The goal is to have $3,200-$3,500 in savings when RoboRide launches.

actions.description: Talk to my nursing program advisor this week about my exact graduation timeline and whether summer clinical slots are available. I need to know the precise number of weeks standing between me and licensure eligibility — not a rough estimate, the actual date. If accelerating by even one rotation block is possible, I want that option on the table.
actions.rationale: My exit from rideshare dependency is the RN license. Everything else — the car payment strategy, the peak-hour scheduling, the savings buffer — is bridge financing. If I can complete clinicals 4-6 weeks earlier by taking an available summer block, that moves up the date I can start earning $58-72K annually. I don't know if acceleration is possible, but I need the information to make the decision. Right now I'm optimizing a bridge without knowing exactly how long the bridge is.
actions.timeline: Advisor meeting this week — I'll ask specifically: What is my projected completion date? Are summer clinical placements available? Is there any outstanding requirement I could front-load?
actions.expected_outcome: Concrete graduation timeline — down to the month. If acceleration is possible, I'll have the specific requirement and cost. If not, I'll know the bridge length and can plan accordingly.

actions.description: Open a small dedicated savings bucket — I'll call it the 'RoboRide Buffer' — and deposit the income above my baseline $413/mo margin into it separately, so I can see it building. This is behavioral accounting, not real accounting, but it prevents me from letting the extra peak-hour earnings absorb into general spending.
actions.rationale: The risk in the next two months is complacency. I'm steady, my stress is low, and the plan is working — which means I could unconsciously start spending the surplus instead of banking it. Labeling the buffer makes it concrete. I've seen nurses in my program panic-quit clinicals over money because they didn't protect their margin during the good months. I'm not doing that. This costs nothing.
actions.timeline: Set up this week — even just a named sub-account or a labeled envelope system in my budgeting app
actions.expected_outcome: Behavioral lock on the savings surplus. When RoboRide launches and driving income softens, I have a named reserve rather than a general savings balance that feels spendable.

decisions.car_payment_strategy: Refinance — with a 796 credit score, I'm carrying a payment rate that predates my creditworthiness. This is fixable this week. I keep the car; I just stop overpaying for it.
decisions.rideshare_volume: Maximize before AV launch — the 8-week window before RoboRide Phase 2 is a known income opportunity. I'll add one high-yield block per week now and scale back only when earnings data shows demand softening in my zones.
decisions.nursing_school_acceleration: Investigate this week — I need my exact graduation date and whether summer clinicals are available. If I can shave 4-6 weeks off the timeline, the bridge gets shorter and the risk window shrinks.
decisions.financial_bridge: Refinancing the car loan is the cleanest first move — it reduces a fixed cost without adding new debt. Personal loan is a secondary option only if refinancing fails and income drops materially after RoboRide launches. I'm not borrowing preemptively against a threat that hasn't materialized yet.

internal_monologue: The car payment number has been bothering me since I did the budget last month — 26% of income on a depreciating asset I need but can't be sentimental about. With a 796 score I should not be paying what I'm paying. That's this week's one concrete task: call the credit union, get the number, move if it makes sense. The RoboRide countdown I can work with — two months is actually enough time to build a real buffer if I'm deliberate. I'm not scared. I'm just doing the math.
